known_differences_from_fetch_script: Year: the script sets year to the FeatureServer item's year, not a date (01_fetch_ottawa.py:147); that 'year' column exists only in raw_cache.parquet, not in a live pull (live columns in the check result lack it, and live/raw_ottawa_sheriff_incidents_2024_2025_2025_fd72af3e5f0e.parquet has no 'year'). The revised contract leaves year_field empty and derives year from CombinedDateTime (epoch_ms, UTC). Recomputed on raw_cache.parquet with pandas (pd.to_datetime(CombinedDateTime, unit='ms', utc=True).dt.year vs year): exactly 1 row differs, OBJECTID 79156, IncidentNumber 2024-12310134, Retail Fraud/Shoplifting (larceny), 2025-01-01 01:24:41 UTC, from the 2024 item. It moves to 2025 and is dropped for 2018-2024, so the replay gives 2024 larceny 1,588 vs the script's 1,589 (README.md:120; 1105 Larceny + 481 Retail Fraud/Shoplifting + 3 Shoplifting with coordinates), a 1/1589 = 0.063% delta, and 14,799 vs 14,800 rows overall; every other year x offense cell is unchanged. The live 2025-2025 pull confirms this row is returned for 2025 (live/raw_ottawa_sheriff_incidents_2024_2025_2025_fd72af3e5f0e.parquet: 1 row, OBJECTID 79156). Converting to America/Detroit instead would move 2 different rows (OBJECTID 1863800 in 2019, 38 in 2021), so UTC is the closer reading.

Date range in where: the script sends no date predicate; it pulls every row of each year's item (01_fetch_ottawa.py:113). The contract's where adds CombinedDateTime >= TIMESTAMP '{start}' AND < TIMESTAMP '{end}'. The service evaluates TIMESTAMP in UTC: the live 2025-2025 pull returned OBJECTID 79156 (2025-01-01 01:24:41 UTC) from the 2024 item and 0 rows from the 2018-2023 items (packet live/*.parquet), so a live 2018-2024 pull omits that one row, consistent with the year derivation above.

Layer ids: the script resolves each item's single layer id live (01_fetch_ottawa.py:97-105, 110-111). The contract hardcodes the ids recorded in README.md:15 (2018=0, 2019=4, 2020=5, 2021=0, 2022=3, 2023=7, 2024=0); if the county republishes an item and the id changes, the contract endpoint breaks where the script would not.

Coordinates: the script derives latitude/longitude from the returned geometry with outSR=4326 (01_fetch_ottawa.py:128, 144-146) and drops only null coordinates (line 178); the contract also drops (0,0). The archived pull has no (0,0) rows (checked: 0) and all 144 Mapped='UnMapped' rows have null latitude, so the kept set is identical (14,800 rows). A live pull must request outSR=4326 for __arcgis_latitude/__arcgis_longitude to be WGS84.

Department scope: the script applies it only server-side (01_fetch_ottawa.py:66, 113). The contract applies it in where and also as a case-sensitive regex condition on every offense rule; on the archived pull all 14,944 rows pass (Department values: Ottawa County Sheriff, OCS-Hudsonville, OCS-Coopersville, OCS-Spring Lake/Ferrysburg).

Block-group join: the script uses a left sjoin and keeps unmatched points (01_fetch_ottawa.py:192); the contract joins with within. README.md:142 reports 14,800/14,800 matched, so no row differs on the archived pull.
Computed field combined_datetime_utc (01_fetch_ottawa.py:166) is not reproduced; it is a derived output column, not a filter.
notes: Translation of 01_fetch_ottawa.py. Offense map copied from OFFENSE_MAP (01_fetch_ottawa.py:71-78): Larceny, Retail Fraud/Shoplifting, Shoplifting -> larceny; Breaking and Entering -> burglary; Stolen Vehicle -> motor_vehicle_theft; Robbery -> robbery. Matching is case_sensitive to mirror the exact dict lookup at line 174. Murder, rape and aggravated_assault have no source category (README.md:59-80), so no rule emits them. Revision: the prior contract used year_field='year', which passed replay (28 cells, 0 failing) but failed the live pull with KeyError 'none of year in the pull'; year_field is now empty so year comes from CombinedDateTime (epoch_ms), which both pulls carry. Recomputed on raw_cache.parquet with pandas: 14,944 rows; IncidentNumber has 14,944 distinct non-null values, so dedupe_on_id=false (the script does not de-duplicate) and true give the same result; 144 rows have null latitude (all Mapped='UnMapped'); kept rows = 14,800, per year 2018 1939, 2019 2073, 2020 2136, 2021 2180, 2022 2254, 2023 2096, 2024 2122; per offense larceny 10,956 (8,089+2,828+39), burglary 2,735, motor_vehicle_theft 1,008, robbery 101. These match README.md:112-121 under the script's item year; with year derived from CombinedDateTime in UTC, 2024 larceny becomes 1,588 and total 14,799 (1 row, OBJECTID 79156, moves to 2025; see known differences). source_kind is cad_dispatch: README.md:6-7 describes an Incident Responses CAD/dispatch feed, not an RMS export. Jurisdictions: the Sheriff patrols unincorporated townships (26:state_nonmunicipal_remainder, 13,751 incidents) and the contract municipalities named by the OCS-* departments (README.md:48): Hudsonville city 2639800 (767), Coopersville city 2618020 (477), Spring Lake village 2675820 (474), Ferrysburg city 2627960 (185). Excluded: Grand Haven city (755), Holland city (90) and Zeeland city (81), which README.md:49-51 lists as served by their own departments, and Norton Shores city (4), Sparta village (4), Casnovia village (2), which fall outside the county. The 755 sheriff-scope points inside Grand Haven city are large relative to the 26 rows with VenueLabel 'Grand Haven City' (raw_cache_profile.json); the evidence does not show whether the Sheriff serves any part of that place, so this exclusion follows the README's agency table. exclusions_stated_by_publisher is empty: the packet contains no statement from the county publisher; the README's block-redacted addresses (README.md:161-164) and excluded categories are observations and repo decisions, not publisher statements.
